دُرَاقِنٌ and دُرَّاقِنٌ, (K, and the latter is mentioned in one of my copies of the S,) the latter is that which is in common use, (TA,) The peach; syn. خَوْخٌ: (AHn, IDrd, K; and so in a copy of the S:) and the apricot; syn. مِشْمِشٌ; (K;) but this application of the words is not known: (TA:) of the Syrian dial.: (K, and so in a copy of the S:) IDrd says that the people of Syria call the former fruit دراقن, which is an arabicized Syrian word, or [rather] Greek, [originally
δωρά� degreesιον ,] and El-Jawáleekee also mentions it among arabicized words. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
